vra:descriptionSet.vra:display: Mirbāṭ near Ṣalālah in the Dhofar Governorate was a port of relative importance in the early-medieval period, trading with India and many other ports in the western Indian Ocean region. However, by the early-twentieth century it had dwindled into a small fishing village. The dispersed settlement formation – similar to many Bāṭinah coastal settlements – developed around a shallow cove, with dwellings to the west of a minor wadī discharge and the Friday mosque, the sūq and the fortlet known as Mirbāṭ Castle gathered beyond the eastern bank of the wadi and close to the sea. A large number of the dwellings are either free-standing or attached to another dwelling, each with its own internal courtyard. The Mirbāṭ dwelling type is distinctive and different from the Bāṭinah coastal examples (e.g., around Ṣuḥār), where a large open space is often found enclosed behind an extensive wall.

vra:description.source: Bandyopadhyay, Soumyen et al, Documentation and Heritage Management and Development Plan: Mirbat, Dhofar Governorate, Liverpool: University of Liverpool, 2017
